intent: Hold the one selected value of a set of MenubarRadioItems.
typical_uses: A sort order or a view mode chosen from a menu

dont_use_when.situation: A set of independent settings, any number of which can be on
A single choice that belongs to a form, shown on the page

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
The item whose `value` is strictly equal (`===`) to the group's value is checked; activating another item reports that item's `value` through `onValueChange`.
Setting `disabled` on the group disables every MenubarRadioItem inside it; an item's own `disabled` can disable that one item further but cannot re-enable it against a disabled group.
The group renders `role="group"` and takes its accessible name from the MenubarLabel inside it, through `aria-labelledby`, unless the caller passes its own `aria-labelledby`.

children.states: children is the group's label and radio items
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

value.states: value is the selected item's value, of any type the caller chooses
value.because: Typed `any` by the primitive, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds; items are matched against it by their own `value`.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the initially selected item's value, of any type the caller chooses
defaultValue.because: Typed `any` by the primitive, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback called with the chosen item's value and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value: any, eventDetails) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A view mode held in the caller's state

bad.title: Selection tracked on each item instead of the group
bad.why: A radio item takes no `checked`; the group's `value` decides which item is checked.
